title: Night audit, i
logline: The desk. The bell. The guests. The ice machine's hum under every panel. The line is suddenly, unmistakably, better.

panels.composition: The Driftwood Motel lobby, 1 AM, drawn in a new hand: architectural, clean, every edge of the desk and the key rack and the vending machine exact. WOOD in the polo. The hum line.

image.prompt: a motel lobby at 1 AM drawn with razor-sharp confident brush-and-ink line and pristine architectural perspective, a night clerk in a maroon polo at the desk, a key rack, a vending machine, a flat hum line beneath the panel, black ink with one gray spot tone
image.notes: Era III's line arrives here. Everything is drawn better and the strip doesn't remark on it.

panels.composition: A GUEST at the desk, a truck driver, needing a room and a receipt. Wood sliding a key across without looking up from the pad.

balloons.text: Twelve. Ice machine's at the end. It doesn't stop.

image.prompt: a truck driver at a motel desk taking a key from a clerk who slides it across without looking up from a drawing pad

panels.composition: The pad: the lobby, drawn in ninety seconds while the guest signed. Better than the lobby.

image.prompt: close-up of a drawing pad with a fast confident ink sketch of a motel lobby, more beautiful than the real one

panels.composition: The lobby empty again. The hum. Wood drawing. The guest's taillights through the glass door. 1:12.

image.prompt: an empty motel lobby at night, a clerk drawing at the desk, taillights receding through the glass door, a flat hum line beneath, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Run 4 begins. The line is Era III's. Nobody says so.
